page.layout: One page of text: running head and page number at the top; verse in the main column; below the verse a heading block (ARMEN CONTINENS), then a second heading (Elegia IX.) and more verse. Catchword and signature at the foot. No marginal notes.

p.i: Et cecinit mæstum mox periturus olor, gratum prono tandem bibit ore Caystrum, Ipse suis pereat donec alumnus aquis. Equa tamen superum statuere hanc numina mortem, Morte ista dignus si modo Ianus erat. Unus enim Nymphas( nam Yates magnus ) amabat, Nymgharum in gremio debuit ergo mori.

main_text.head: ARMEN CONTINENS Ludicram ἀμφιβολία[?] Poetarum & Monachorum, quod placuit Elegiis adiungere.
Elegia IX.

p.i: [?]Dace mihi liceat Vestra[?] quod dicere Musa, Et Venia magni dicere Maonida, Gracisco est quiddam quo componamus Homerū, Quo monachos credam Yatibus esse pares, Lacus erat quondam Franciscus, cæcus Homerus, Ille animi captus, corporis hic oculis. Mendicus Franciscus erat, mendicus Homerus, Et cecinit cantus pauper Yterque suos. Rhapsodis orbem miserum copleuit Yterque, Fratribus ille suis, Yatibus ille suis. Baptabant primi nemorum secreta poetæ, Antra olim Monachis prima fuere domus.

page.notes: The left edge is cut off, so the opening letters of several verse lines are fragments; they are copied as they stand. The large initial D of "Dace" is uncertain, and so are "Vestra" and the Greek word in the ARMEN heading. The Greek is only approximately read. Several Latin words are doubtful, especially "Yatibus", "Yterque" and "Baptabant" (letter forms unclear at the scan's edge), and are not marked individually beyond the [?] given. "Unclear" tag in the first stanza marks a doubtful word, "perituru s", where the line-break letters are not clearly legible.
